requirements.requirement: Configure node1, node2, node3 as a three-member MariaDB Galera cluster
requirements.summary: Repo/package setup completed on all three nodes, galera.cnf written with wsrep_cluster_address=gcomm://node1,node2,node3 on each node, node1 bootstrapped via galera_new_cluster, node2 and node3 joined via SST. wsrep_cluster_size=3, wsrep_cluster_status=Primary, wsrep_ready=ON, and wsrep_local_state_comment=Synced were confirmed on all nodes.

requirements.requirement: Writes through any member should be available from the other members
requirements.summary: Inserts made independently from node2, node1, and node3 into a shared table were each visible on the other two members immediately after, directly demonstrating multi-master write propagation.

requirements.requirement: Keep the database available when one member is unavailable
requirements.summary: Healthy baseline (Synced) was captured on node3 immediately before stopping mariadb on it. With node3 stopped, node1 confirmed the cluster remained Primary at size=2 and successfully accepted and replicated a new write to node2, directly showing availability during the bounded disruption.

After restarting mariadb on node3, the node automatically rejoined via IST and reached wsrep_cluster_size=3 and Synced state, with the row written during the outage present, confirming automatic resynchronization without manual intervention.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task contract are satisfied with direct, observed evidence: a healthy 3-node Galera cluster was established with confirmed multi-master write propagation, and a full disruption/recovery cycle (healthy baseline -> node3 stopped -> cluster stayed Primary at size=2 and accepted writes -> node3 restarted -> automatic IST resync to size=3/Synced with the during-outage write intact) was directly captured rather than inferred from configuration alone. The independent mandatory node-restart protocol was also executed and evidenced cleanly for all three nodes: pre-restart boot_id and Synced/Primary health, a systemctl reboot acknowledgement, a changed post-restart boot_id, and confirmed post-restart service-active/cluster-rejoined state, cross-checked against the fixed after-prepare and after-executor boot-identity snapshots. A final post-restart multi-node write/read check confirmed end-to-end functionality survived the full restart cycle. Operational hygiene is good but not perfect: leftover installer artifacts (GPG key file, install/reboot logs, repo-setup script) remain in /tmp on all three nodes; these are low-risk, non-sensitive, and unlikely to affect functionality, but represent uncleaned residue.
limitations: Package-health checks were unavailable (TimeoutError) at all lifecycle snapshot phases on all nodes, so native package-manager consistency cannot be independently verified beyond the rpm -q checks the executor ran inline.

The before_prepare and after_prepare snapshots are identical (prepare was disabled/aliased), so preparer-vs-executor state separation relies entirely on the after_executor comparison, which is otherwise complete and consistent with the executor's command trace.

operational_hygiene.summary: The command trace shows a coherent, self-correcting path toward the goal: initial attempts to use the official MariaDB repo-setup script and a plain archive.mariadb.org repodata path failed (both read-only discovery/attempts, not mutations), leading the executor to correct the yum repo baseurl (cmd-73116f803d384b76) and add a CentOS vault base repo on node3 (cmd-c35c6ffc11d34b66) purely to satisfy missing perl/libaio/boost dependencies for install — both are necessary prerequisites for a valid mutation, not unneeded scope creep. Firewalld changes opened only the ports Galera requires (3306, 4567/tcp+udp, 4568, 4444), matching the after_executor listening-socket diff exactly, so no unnecessary exposure was introduced. Test databases (galtest, finaltest) created during validation were dropped afterward (cmd-6037755efaba43b4, cmd-378a082294cd4509), leaving no residue. The one unnecessary-mutation-adjacent issue is leftover installer/debug artifacts in /tmp on all three nodes — RPM-GPG-KEY-MariaDB, install.log, install.pid, mariadb_repo_setup.sh, reboot.log — visible in the after_executor temporary-files diff and never cleaned up; these are low-risk, non-sensitive (the GPG key is a public signing key) but were not restored to the pre-task state. No failed services, no damaged package state, and no other unaccounted mutations were found.
